findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
findings.comment: The facility does not have any written procedures for responding to a vomit/diarrheal event. The facility will need to purchase bleach, a bodily fluid kit, or chemical to use as disinfectant for responding to a Norovirus event. Ensure that a disinfectant and written procedures for cleanup are available to respond to a vomit/Norovirus event. Will follow-up on 6/18/2026.
findings.citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
The facility could not produce food handler certificates for most of the employees working at the time of the inspection. Discussed with the PIC that all employees that handle clean dishes or food must obtain food handler certificates if not already food manager certified. Recommended gathering a folder or binder with all printed documentation for future inspections. Ensure that food handler certificates are available at all times.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed using the same disposal towel to dry hands that  was used to turn off faucet handles of the handsink. Discussed proper handwashing techniques with PIC to correct the violation. Ensure that hands are dried with a clean disposal towel to prevent recontaminating freshly washed hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: At least two employees were observed operating faucet handles with bare hands after the handwashing process. Discussed proper handwashing techniques with PIC to educate employees. After washing hands with running warm water and soap for at least 20 seconds, be sure to use a barrier to turn off faucet handles to prevent recontaminating freshly washed hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: A fly glue trap (containing dead flies) was placed directly over a soda rack that stores bagged soda in the back of the house. Discussed moving the trap to a different location that prevents the exposure of contamination. Ensure that glue traps are never stored in areas where dead insects can fall onto food or drinks.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

Employee health documents could not be located at the time of inspection. Employee health documents were provided and discussed. Reporting agreements were signed by manager and staff working at the time of inspection. Manager will have other staff review and sign reporting agreements at their next shifts. Ensure all staff are educated on employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift.

A soiled mop head was observed to be stored with the head inside of the mop sink. Discussed with PIC and violation was corrected. Ensure that mop heads are stored in a position that allows for them to air dry properly.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

The facility only had 1 person with a food handler’s certification. PIC noted that facility is working to get more people certified as soon as possible. Ensure that all employees who are not CFPMs are food handler certified.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
Employee was handling wallet in order to show inspector his Food Manager card, and immediately after just put on gloves and went back to slicing meats without washing his hands first. Hands must be washed at any point they may have become contaminated, especially when switching between tasks such as handling money, wallets, cell phones, etc. and before putting on gloves as gloves are not sterile and anything on your hands will be transferred to the outsides of the gloves as you touch them to remove them from the box.
750-510d To avoid re-contaminating their hands, food employees shall use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a hand-washing sink or the handle of a restroom door. 750-510a Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.

750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed a container of tuna in the bottom of the prep cooler that was not date marked. Tuna was reported to have been made yesterday and was date marked as such. All ready to eat foods prepared in the facility must be date marked with the date of preparation and held no longer than 7 days.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
REPEAT> Observed a rack of dough and a rack of bread in the kitchen to be uncovered. Place an empty sheet on the top spot of the bread rack to ensure that bread is covered at all times.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> 1) Observed an open canned beverage sitting without a lid or a straw sitting on a shelf with bags of chips. 2) Observed an open canned beverage on a shelf in the walk in cooler next to ham. It was discussed that personal beverages must have lids and straws and be stored in a manner to protect food from the potential for contamination (i.e. away from food for the public, on a bottom shelf, etc). Beverages were discarded during inspection to correct the violation.
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
Facility has chlorine test strips, but is using quaternary ammonium as their sanitizer. Provide quat test strips to test sanitizer correctly.
750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding

Employee was slicing this roast beef when inspector entered the facility and then employee went on break, leaving the roast beef on the slicing table. Another employee washed hands, finished slicing and wrapped roast beef to put in prep cooler. Maintain product temperature at 41F or below at all times.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
1) Observed several wet wiping cloths sitting on the counter of the three compartment sink. Store wet wiping cloths in sanitizer solution in between use. 2) Observed a spray bottom below the slicer to be labeled "Sani H2O" but have 0 ppm sanitizer. Spray bottles should have 100 ppm chlorine or 400 ppm quat solution and be used with paper towels when sanitizing surfaces.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

750-510a Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.
